        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated),

        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The study focuses on the "Evaluation of Spatial Abilities within a 2D Auditory Platform Game" which "conveys 2D spatial relationships via audio alone." While it is "based on the same concepts as the early Super Mario Bros. platform games," indicating a fun element, the design heavily borrows from "sonification to create effective audio cues that guide a player." This suggests that the primary utilitarian mechanic (conveying spatial relationships via audio for evaluation) was designed first, using a game format as the vehicle, aligning with 'mostly utility first'.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: The study design is both symmetrical and asymmetrical. It is symmetrical because all participants played the same game levels and performed the same task of describing the level layout to create mental maps. It is asymmetrical because the participants were divided into three distinct groups based on their visual ability (sighted vs. visually impaired) and the version of the game they played (audio-visual vs. audio-only).
